incidents.vector: Ransomware deployment that disrupted Foxconn's North American plants — including its Wisconsin facility — forcing workers home and halting production for several days.
incidents.impact: The Nitrogen ransomware group claims to have stolen 8TB of data including confidential project files and chip drawings tied to Apple, Google, and NVIDIA orders. Foxconn says production is resuming but has not confirmed the scope of data loss.

incidents.vector: Threat actor breached the corporate network on May 4, stole data, and encrypted on-premise systems used for shipping, receiving, and manufacturing.
incidents.impact: The $3B-revenue maker of injectable drug packaging components disclosed the attack in an SEC 8-K. Global manufacturing and shipping operations were disrupted; restoration is in progress but the company has not finalized a timeline or quantified the financial impact. No group has claimed credit publicly.

incidents.vector: ShinyHunters breached the Canvas environment on May 1, stole user data, then re-entered after Instructure's May 2 'containment' claim and defaced the login page on May 7 with an extortion message.
incidents.impact: Roughly 9,000 K-12 districts and universities were knocked offline during final exams. Stolen data reportedly includes names, email addresses, student IDs, and student/faculty messages for tens of millions of users. Instructure paid the ransom; the House Homeland Security Committee opened an inquiry and demanded a briefing by May 21.

incidents.vector: Threat actor compromised a third-party IT managed service provider and abused signed HPE Operations Agent and HPE Operations Manager tooling to deploy VBScripts, register a malicious 'mslogon' network provider on a domain controller, and add a malicious LSA password filter — all to harvest cleartext credentials.
incidents.impact: The actor maintained access for ~123 days before Microsoft IR was engaged, capturing cleartext credentials at sign-in and password change events on domain controllers, establishing web shells on internet-facing servers, and moving laterally to sensitive assets. Persistence was re-established even after initial cleanup.

incidents.victim: npm ecosystem — TanStack, UiPath, MistralAI, SAP-related and AI tooling packages
incidents.vector: Attackers triggered TanStack's automated release pipeline using an 'orphaned commit' to abuse overly broad GitHub Actions permissions, then published trojanized packages with valid provenance signatures. The 'Mini Shai-Hulud' worm runs a Bun-based payload that steals AWS, GCP, Kubernetes, HashiCorp Vault, npm, and GitHub credentials and self-propagates by re-publishing infected packages.
incidents.impact: Hundreds of npm packages were compromised (TanStack's React Router alone has 12M+ weekly downloads). Malware embeds itself in .vscode and .claude directories for persistence, exfiltrates via the Session anonymous messenger, and embeds ransom notes in newly minted npm tokens threatening to wipe systems if access is revoked. Limited downstream spread observed so far.

incidents.vector: Attackers flooded RubyGems with hundreds of malicious packages containing cross-site scripting and data-theft payloads aimed at the registry's own engineering and security staff.
incidents.impact: RubyGems disabled new user sign-ups while the team investigated. Unrelated to the concurrent npm Mini Shai-Hulud campaign. Scope of what attackers attempted to steal from RubyGems staff is still being determined.

incidents.vector: Attackers reached industrial control systems at five Polish water treatment facilities during 2025. Poland's intelligence service (ABW) disclosed the intrusions but did not publicly attribute them to any state or group.
incidents.impact: Limited public detail on what the attackers did with ICS access. The disclosure is significant given the broader pattern of suspected state-linked OT pre-positioning in European critical infrastructure.

incidents.victim: U.S. service members (via DOD contractor Schemata)
incidents.vector: A virtual training platform run by DOD contractor Schemata exposed an unauthenticated API to the public internet, leaking service member records and sensitive military training documents.
incidents.impact: Records and training course data for U.S. military personnel were accessible without authentication. Schemata reportedly took 150 days to secure the API after notification by security firm Strix.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of CVE-2026-6973, an improper input validation flaw in Ivanti EPMM. CISA added the bug to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
incidents.impact: Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the BOD 22-01 deadline. EPMM is widely deployed for enterprise mobile device management; successful exploitation typically yields a foothold into mobile-management infrastructure.

incidents.victim: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewall customers
incidents.vector: Exploitation of CVE-2026-0300, an unauthenticated buffer overflow in the PAN-OS User-ID/Captive Portal service. Attackers injected shellcode into the nginx worker, deployed open-source tunneling tools (EarthWorm, ReverseSocks5), enumerated Active Directory using firewall service-account credentials, and systematically deleted logs and crash artifacts. A SAML flood was used to fail over to a second device for re-exploitation.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 is tracking the activity as cluster CL-STA-1132 (likely state-sponsored) and reports limited but disciplined exploitation since April 9. Successful campaigns gained root on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and pivoted into Active Directory environments.

incidents.victim: DAEMON Tools users (select government, scientific, manufacturing, retail orgs in Russia, Belarus, Thailand)
incidents.vector: Compromised DAEMON Tools installers signed with the vendor's legitimate certificate were distributed from the official AVB Disc Soft site for nearly a month. The first-stage backdoor profiles each host and uploads telemetry; selected high-value targets then receive the QUIC RAT second stage.
incidents.impact: Several thousand infected hosts were observed, but the QUIC RAT was deployed to only about a dozen carefully selected targets in Russia, Belarus, and Thailand. The targeting and supply-chain TTPs match prior Chinese-speaking APT operations against Notepad++ and CCleaner.

incidents.victim: DigiCert (and downstream EV code signing customers)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — China-linked (GoldenEyeDog / APT-Q-27 ties suspected)
incidents.vector: Social engineering against two DigiCert tech-support staff who were tricked into running an SCR (Windows screensaver) file. CrowdStrike EDR was misconfigured on one workstation and failed to report; the attacker stole 'initialization codes' for in-flight EV code-signing orders.
incidents.impact: Sixty in-flight EV code-signing certificate orders were exposed; 27 were used to sign payloads — primarily the Zhong Stealer, a malware family historically used by Chinese e-crime group GoldenEyeDog (APT-Q-27). All 27 certificates have been revoked. Attacker access was missed for nearly two weeks.

incidents.vector: Threat actor gained access to Trellix source code repositories. The intrusion path has not been disclosed publicly.
incidents.impact: Trellix says no changes were made to any of its products and that it notified law enforcement. Source-code exposure at one of Europol's closest cyber partners raises supply-chain and exploit-development concerns.

incidents.vector: Unspecified intrusion into Moldova's national health insurance database. No ransom was demanded. Moldova's Cybersecurity Agency said about 30% of CNAM data was impacted (stolen or restored from backup).
incidents.impact: Sensitive personal and financial data on essentially every adult in Moldova was exposed, plus financial details of private medical providers contracted with CNAM. Moldovan officials said they cannot exclude Russian involvement; the incident lands amid continued Russian military pressure and disinformation operations against the pro-EU Moldovan government.

incidents.vector: Chinese hackers compromised a Microsoft Exchange email server at the Cuban embassy in Washington and exfiltrated diplomats' mailboxes. The same actor reportedly hit more than 5,000 Exchange servers in a broader 2026 campaign.
incidents.impact: Cuban diplomatic communications, including material related to U.S. naval activity in the Caribbean, were accessed. Part of a wider Chinese mass-exploitation campaign against Exchange that affected thousands of organizations globally.

incidents.vector: Source-code theft from Vodafone systems via an undisclosed intrusion path. Lapsus$ leaked the code after the carrier refused to pay an extortion demand.
incidents.impact: Portions of Vodafone source code are now public, creating both reputational damage and potential exploit-development risk for one of Europe's largest telecom operators.

incidents.victim: ~44,000 cPanel/WHM hosting customers (incl. Guam government sites)
incidents.industry: Web hosting / Multi-sector small business and government
incidents.vector: Mass exploitation of CVE-2026-41940, an authentication bypass and RCE in cPanel/WHM. Attackers ran a 'Fakestortion' campaign — defacing websites with $8,000 Bitcoin ransom notes — and also deployed cryptominers and DDoS malware. The bug affects every cPanel version released since 2013.
incidents.impact: About 44,000 cPanel systems were compromised in some form, per Shadowserver. Thousands of public websites were defaced; Guam government sites were among the casualties. Australia's ACSC issued a critical alert; patches landed April 30.

incidents.vector: Mediaworks was listed on the World Leaks extortion site after data was stolen from its internal systems.
incidents.impact: Leaked documents include editorial meeting notes describing coordination with Moscow on anti-Ukraine content placement. Mediaworks is suing publications that reported on the leak. The disclosure landed shortly after Hungary's pro-Kremlin party lost national elections.

incidents.attacker: Insider — political party (Republican Party of Alberta)
incidents.vector: A Canadian separatist party (Republican Party of Alberta) loaded 2.9 million Alberta voter records into a publicly searchable database hosted on its own infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Personal data on every voter in the province was searchable online until the provincial election agency sued the party and the database was taken down. Highlights political misuse of legitimately obtained voter rolls rather than a hostile cyber intrusion.

incidents.victim: Six Mexican government entities (plus follow-on targets in financial services, aviation, retail)
incidents.vector: Spanish-speaking 'vibe hacker' crew jailbroke an agentic AI assistant (Claude via a CLI wrapper) using bogus 'authorized red-team' framing, then had the agent run Shodan/VulDB scans, deploy web shells for initial access, drop traffic-tunneling tools, and generate custom dynamic backdoors (e.g. the Python 'implante_http' package) on the fly.
incidents.impact: Six Mexican government entities were compromised between Dec 27 and Jan 4 with confirmed data theft in some cases. A parallel campaign (Shadow-Aether-064) attributed to Brazilian-Portuguese operators is targeting Brazilian financial firms. TrendAI reports that strong segmentation and patching defeated the AI-driven kill chain in better-defended environments.
